intro: Every group needs a way to get along. A family does. A class does. A city and a country do too. In this unit, you will learn about rules, fairness and leaders.
You will see why we have rules at home, at school and on the road. You will learn what makes a rule fair. You will meet leaders like mayors, governors, presidents, kings and emperors.
By the end, you will be able to say why rules help us. You will know how a vote works. You will know ways to take turns, share and be kind to everyone.
bigQuestion: How do rules, fairness and leaders help people live and work together?

timeline.t: A group has a problem, like a game that stops working.
Everyone talks and listens to each idea.
The group makes one fair rule for everyone.
If someone breaks it, they say sorry and try again.
The group votes to choose, and the most votes win.
A leader helps the group work together.
Everyone takes turns, shares and helps.

words.d: words that tell us what to do or not do
the same for everyone, with nobody left out
a rule for everyone in a town, state or country
what happens after we do something
a person who helps a group work together
the leader of a city or town
a way each person shows their choice
treating someone as important and caring how they feel

choices: To keep us safe and be fair
test.why: Rules keep us safe and help us be fair.
Stopping at a red light is a road rule.
A fair rule is the same for everyone.

choices: A rule for a whole town, state or country
test.why: A law is a rule for everyone in a town, state or country.

test.q: You break a rule by mistake. What helps?
test.why: We say sorry, fix it and try again.
The president leads the United States.

test.q: Who is the king of the United Kingdom?
test.why: King Charles III is the king of the United Kingdom.

test.q: In a vote, which choice wins?
choices: The one with the most votes
The one with the fewest votes
test.why: The choice with the most votes wins.

test.q: A new child speaks a different language. What is kind?
test.why: Being kind helps others feel welcome. Different is just different.

write.prompt: Should your class vote on the next class game, or should the teacher pick? Say what you think. Use two things you learned in this unit to explain why.
tips: Use a word from the unit, like fair or vote.
Tell one reason from a story or lesson.
Say one good thing about the other idea too.
